description: Grade 5 example: write an interval under a key signature (D major, treble clef).

provenance.authoredBy: Music Theory Path curriculum team (Brief 10 addendum)

item.prompt: The key signature of D major is shown. Write the note a major 6th up from this note, adding an accidental only if the key signature does not already give it.

music.textAlternative: One minim, F#4, under the key signature of D major.

hints: Find the letter name first, then decide what the interval needs on that letter.
Then compare with the key signature: write a sign only for the difference.

feedback.correct: Correct. F♯ up a major 6th is D♯. D major has only F♯ and C♯, so D is natural in the signature and the D♯ needs its own sharp sign.

mistakes.redundant-or-missing-accidental: F♯ up a major 6th is D♯. D major has only F♯ and C♯, so D is natural in the signature and the D♯ needs its own sharp sign.
mistakes.accidental-not-applied: Check what the key signature already gives that letter before adding a sign. F♯ up a major 6th is D♯. D major has only F♯ and C♯, so D is natural in the signature and the D♯ needs its own sharp sign.
mistakes.enharmonic-spelling: That sounds the same but uses the wrong letter name. An interval's number fixes the letter: count the letter names from the starting note.

feedback.fallback: F♯ up a major 6th is D♯. D major has only F♯ and C♯, so D is natural in the signature and the D♯ needs its own sharp sign.
